title: cost-optimization: autotune defaults for batching/caching, quantization profiles, and unit-econ tooling
author: Ava Morgan
description: Adds an end-to-end cost-optimization automation bundle: (1) new autotune defaults for batching and KV-cache recommendations driven by workload profiles, (2) quantization profile catalog and selection heuristics for common model families, and (3) initial unit-economics (uecon) CLI and dashboard plumbing to evaluate per-token cost impact. Motivation: teams repeatedly tune batching/caching/quant by hand; this provides safe defaults, automated experiments, and tooling to reason about unit economics. Changes include a runtime-safe autotuner with conservative rollout policies, quant profiles exported from offline benchmark harness, and a uecon CLI that computes per-route cost projections using observed token distributions. Includes docs, unit tests, and e2e canary against perf-canary. Related: ENG-4218 (autotune), PM-214 (cost-optimization roadmap). Checklist: - [x] runtime changes covered by unit and integration tests - [x] conservative defaults gated behind feature flag - [x] docs and migration notes - [x] e2e canary run and smoke validation
commits_summary: feat(autotune): implement conservative batching and caching defaults with workload profiling
feat(quant): add quantization profile catalog + selection heuristics
feat(uecon): add initial uecon CLI and cost projection library
chore(ci): enable perf-canary e2e job for autotune canary
docs: add cost-optimization/autotune guide and migration notes
test: add unit and integration tests for autotune and quant selection
review_conversation: Diego Ramos (reviewer): Can you expand on the safety guarantees for the autotuner? Need clarity on how rollouts avoid regressions under unexpected token distributions.

Ava Morgan (author): Autotuner defaults are conservative: initial profile is applied only when >95% of recent windows match a profile and we apply a canary route with 1% traffic. We fall back instantly to baseline on any QoS spike. Added details in docs and comments in engine.py.
Priya Nair (reviewer): The quant selection heuristics look good but we need an escape hatch for older NV setups that don't support the new kernels.
Ava Morgan (author): Added kernel compatibility checks and a config flag to pin legacy quant mode; tests added to cover both paths.
Ethan Park (reviewer): CI showed a flaky test (test_canary_smoke) in the first run; re-run fixed it but please add a retry or more deterministic assertion.
Ava Morgan (author): Added a stricter assertion on observed latency window and retry logic in the canary smoke test. CI re-ran and all checks passed.
Diego Ramos (reviewer): Approving pending small docs phrasing nit; confirmed canary metrics in perf-canary dashboard look OK after merge preview.
Priya Nair (reviewer): LGTM. Will follow up with SRE on alert thresholds for autotuner rollbacks.
release_notes: Introduce autotune conservative defaults for batching and KV-cache, quantization profile catalog with selection heuristics, and initial unit-economics tooling (CLI + reporting). Feature gated behind feature flag 'cost_autotune_v1'. Improves median token-cost by up to 18% in internal canaries for conversational workloads without QoS regressions.
